quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds can remember every flower they've visited and how long it will take each one to refill with nectar. These tiny birds also have incredible memories for migration routes, returning to the exact same feeders year after year, sometimes within days of their previous arrival date!

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Butterflies in Your Garden
short_read.teaser: Butterflies taste with their feet and can see colors we can't even imagine. This delightful article reveals the hidden world of these gentle garden visitors.

medium_read.title: The Women Who Mapped the Ocean Floor
medium_read.teaser: Marie Tharp's hand-drawn maps in the 1950s revealed underwater mountains and valleys no one knew existed, changing our understanding of Earth forever. Her story is one of persistence, artistry, and scientific brilliance.

long_read.title: The Enduring Traditions of Hungarian Folk Art
long_read.teaser: From intricate embroidery to vibrant pottery, Hungarian folk art tells stories passed down through generations. This beautiful exploration celebrates the artisans keeping these traditions alive today.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season
port_angeles.description: Late July is peak pupping season for harbor seals along the Strait of Juan de Fuca! Mother seals give birth on rocky beaches and sandbars, and pups can swim within hours of being born. You might spot them hauled out on rocks near Ediz Hook or along the shoreline.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power those amazing wings!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! It's about 1,200 beats per minute — faster than we can even imagine!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Their hearts beat an astonishing 1,200 times per minute! That's about 20 times per second to fuel their hovering flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To support this incredibly fast heartbeat, hummingbirds must eat half their body weight in sugar each day, visiting hundreds of flowers from dawn to dusk.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Barbara! Pillangó is such a lovely, dancing word for such a lovely creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: It's 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound like something fluttering? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and napfény means sunshine!)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language unrelated to most European languages, belonging instead to the Finno-Ugric family. It's known for its beautiful, melodic sound and complex but logical structure.

puzzle_3.question: What do Olympic marmots do for about eight months of the year?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! These charming creatures hibernate through the long mountain winters, cuddled together in family groups to stay warm.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: They actually hibernate for about eight months! Olympic marmots are only active during the brief mountain summer, making the most of the warm months.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Olympic marmots are found nowhere else on Earth except the Olympic Peninsula. These social animals live in colonies and greet each other by touching noses!
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Meet the marmots — Olympic National Park
